title: Cloudflare builds Kitesurf as a lighter browser for AI agents
friendlyTitle: Cloudflare makes a smaller web browser for AI agents
summary: Cloudflare introduced Kitesurf, a browser engine designed for agents that runs in WebAssembly on Workers rather than launching Chromium. It is available free during beta through Browser Run and supports common automation interfaces while prioritizing isolation, structured output and lower resource use.
friendlySummary: Kitesurf gives agents a web browser without running a full copy of Chrome. It is designed to use less computing power and start each session in isolation.
whyItMatters: Browser instances are a major cost and security boundary for web-using agents. A smaller stateless runtime could make parallel automation cheaper, but teams should test website compatibility, prompt-injection defenses and failure behavior before moving production tasks.
friendlyWhyItMatters: This may make web automation cheaper and safer. Test it carefully because some websites may not work exactly as they do in Chrome.
